sections.heading: How Our Roofing Contractors Perform Built-Up Roofing

runs.v: Membrane, Surfacing, and Drainage Assessment

c.v: Newark Quality Roofing contractors assess the membrane, surfacing, flashing details, and drainage before specifying a built-up roof, because each fails on a different timeline.

runs.v: Proper drainage design is essential to prevent water pooling on BUR roofs, and existing roof conditions must be verified before installing BUR to ensure structural capacity, because the heavy weight of BUR requires robust structural support.
Multi-Ply BUR Construction

c.v: Newark Quality Roofing builds BUR from alternating plies of reinforcing fabric and hot bitumen, each fully mopped ply adding an independent waterproofing layer.

runs.v: Fiberglass fabric raises fire performance and dimensional stability; polyester raises elongation for a deck that moves. Hot-mopped asphalt installation requires skilled labor and specialized equipment and can produce strong odors that require safety precautions.
Restoration, Recover, and Conversion

c.v: Newark Quality Roofing restores a sound BUR roof by resurfacing rather than replacing it, the lower-cost path when the plies hold.

runs.v: Restoration consolidates the gravel, repairs damaged areas, and applies new surfacing or a reflective coating, per NRCA maintenance guidance.

sections.heading: A Roofing System Built for Newark's Weather

runs.v: BUR systems can last 20 to 30 years with proper maintenance, a long term performance record set by the weather. BUR can experience thermal shock from extreme temperature fluctuations, so hybrid systems add a polymer-modified bitumen cap sheet for flexibility through freeze-thaw cycles. Light-colored gravel or mineral aggregate reflects sunlight and prevents UV degradation, and aggregate-surfaced BUR provides fire resistance; smooth BUR has a top layer without aggregate for easier inspection and takes a reflective coating that reduces heat absorption for energy efficiency. Seasonal inspections, in spring, fall, and after storm damage from wind, help identify potential issues before they worsen, protect the plies, and keep the property protected.

c.v: Newark Quality Roofing maintains, repairs, and resurfaces residential built-up roofs across Essex County on older flat-roof homes, apartment buildings, and mixed-use properties.

runs.v: Replacing the roof covering on a detached one- and two-family dwelling is ordinary maintenance under N.J.A.C. 5:23-2.7, with no construction permit.
On mid-twentieth-century Essex County buildings, a residential job means gravel redistribution, drain clearing, and resurfacing, or a new BUR system, EPDM, or TPO at end of life.

c.v: Newark Quality Roofing installs and restores commercial built-up roofing across Essex County on warehouses, industrial facilities, and buildings with heavy rooftop equipment, using 3-ply to 5-ply systems, with extra plies for maximum protection.

runs.v: A dropped tool that punctures a single-ply membrane only dents the gravel-armored surface, so BUR roofs have high durability against foot traffic and debris and stand up to service access. Aging roofs get 3 options, replacement, restoration, or single-ply conversion, so businesses can plan commercial roofing around operations.

sections.heading: BUR vs. Modified Bitumen and Single-Ply Commercial Roofing Systems

runs.v: Multiple-ply construction gives BUR better durability and impact resistance, and BUR offers good fire performance with high fire-resistance ratings. The trade-offs are weight and labor: BUR installation complexity results in higher labor costs than single-ply systems. Modified bitumen builds similar redundancy from factory rolls; TPO and EPDM are lighter seamed sheets. Local appropriateness of BUR depends on existing building types and climate exposure, so building type and rooftop traffic decide between built up systems and lighter roofing systems.

sections.heading: Our Built-Up Roofing Process, Step by Step

items.v: Assessment and System Design
A Newark Quality Roofing technician assesses the roof, then specifies the ply count, fabric, bitumen grade, and surfacing against the ¼-inch-per-foot minimum slope, per NRCA and ARMA.
Written Estimate and Permitting
A Newark Quality Roofing written estimate sets the scope, materials, and schedule, and the permit is filed when a commercial project needs one under N.J.A.C. 5:23-2.7.
Deck Preparation
A Newark Quality Roofing crew removes the existing roof or prepares it for recover, repairs the deck, and installs tapered insulation that creates the drainage slope, plus a cover board.
Ply and Surfacing Construction
A Newark Quality Roofing crew mops reinforcing-fabric plies in hot bitumen, creating redundant waterproofing, then embeds gravel in a flood coat or applies a reflective coating, per NRCA.
Flashing and Detail Work
A Newark Quality Roofing crew details penetrations, edges, and curbs with cant strips and termination bars, sealing the seams and transitions, per NRCA flashing guidance.
Verification, Cleanup, and Warranty

A Newark Quality Roofing lead verifies adhesion, flashing, and drainage, clears the work area, and issues a written workmanship warranty on the labor, separate from the manufacturer material warranty.

sections.heading: Repair, Restore, or Replace? Built-Up Roofing Services in New Jersey

c.v: BUR repairs are generally less expensive than a single-ply membrane replacement, and restoration costs a fraction of full replacement while the plies hold.

faqs.q: How long does a built-up roof last?

runs.v: 30 years on the InterNACHI life-expectancy chart, longer than EPDM, TPO, or modified bitumen.

faqs.q: Why choose built-up roofing over a single-ply membrane?

runs.v: For multi-ply redundancy, impact resistance, and a 30-year service life against 7–20 years for TPO.

faqs.q: Should you restore or replace a built-up roof?

runs.v: Restore it when the plies hold and damage stays localized; replace it when damage exceeds 25–30% of the membrane or leaks recur at the same detail.

faqs.q: Do you need a permit for a commercial built-up roof in Newark, NJ?

runs.v: Yes, past New Jersey's 25% rule: repairing more than 25% of the roof area in 12 months requires a permit under N.J.A.C. 5:23-2.7.

faqs.q: How much does built-up roofing cost in Essex County, NJ?

runs.v: Typically $7–$12 per square foot installed and $2.50–$10 per square foot for repair; Newark Quality Roofing provides a free estimate.

faqs.q: Can a built-up roof be converted to a single-ply membrane?

runs.v: Yes. Newark Quality Roofing strips the BUR to the deck, upgrades the insulation, and installs EPDM or TPO.

faqs.q: Are built-up roofs better than shingles?

runs.v: They suit different roofs: codes allow asphalt shingles only on slopes of 2:12 or steeper, while BUR is made for flat and low-slope roofs.

faqs.q: What is another name for built-up roofing?

runs.v: BUR, tar-and-gravel roofing, or a hot-mopped roof.
